_why: UnifiedTable::column_names() is used by callers as 'the RELATION's column set' — notably the OUTER-join null-pad paths in stream_table_join.rs (the pre-existing LEFT-join no-match pad, and the EmitWithNulls arm after #2025). But OptimizedTableImpl::column_names() (unified_table.rs:2844) reads ONLY self.column_indexes — the union of columns OBSERVED in ingested rows. It never consults self.schema, which set_schema populates (unified_table.rs:1829) and which schema() already returns (:2836). A table created WITH a schema but which has not yet loaded any rows therefore returns []. An unmatched OUTER row against such a table is padded with NO table columns, and a legal t.col reference fails to resolve even though the declared schema says col exists. The default trait impl (:307) has the same hole: it unions iter_records() keys and likewise ignores an attached schema. Before #2025 the EmitWithNulls arm papered over this by fabricating id/name/value — for a table that genuinely had id/name, two were accidentally right. #2025 removed the fabrication (correctly — that is the class #2000 deleted), which makes this root cause VISIBLE rather than masked. This fix also improves the pre-existing LEFT-join pad, which is why it is not #2025's to make.

anchors._note: TWO in this file: the DEFAULT trait impl (:307, unions iter_records keys) and the OptimizedTableImpl override (:2844, reads column_indexes). BOTH ignore an attached schema; both are in scope.

TWO: the trait declaration and the OptimizedTableImpl impl at unified_table.rs:2836 — the accessor that already exposes what column_names must union in. It is a TRAIT method, so the default impl can consult it generically.
the consumer that motivates the fix: the LEFT-join no-match pad and the EmitWithNulls arm. Its own comment already states the contract — 'the RELATION's full column union, not one sampled row'.

blast_radius._note: 31 refs / 11 files across src/ tests/ examples/. Only unified_table.rs is EDITED; every other file is a call site or an existing test whose behaviour must not regress.

tests._note: fail_to_pass name indicative. REQUIRED and DISCRIMINATING: construct an OptimizedTableImpl, call set_schema with a schema declaring a column, ingest NO rows, assert column_names() contains that column. It MUST be verified to FAIL against master (which returns []). A second test covering the observed-plus-declared UNION (a row carrying a column the schema does not declare, plus a declared column no row carries) is required — a fix that REPLACES observed with declared instead of unioning would pass the first test and be wrong.

acceptance: OptimizedTableImpl::column_names() returns the UNION of column_indexes keys and the attached schema's field names, sorted and deduplicated
the DEFAULT trait impl (unified_table.rs:307) unions the attached schema's field names too — Table and CompactTable use it and have the identical hole
when NO schema is attached, behaviour is unchanged: observed-only is correct in that case
the union is a union, not a replacement — a column present in ingested rows but absent from the schema is still reported

the doc comments on both impls are updated to state that the result is observed-union-declared, not observed-only; the existing default-impl doc block explicitly promises correlated-subquery callers a complete set and must not now be misleading

decorrelated_index.rs's two overrides are ASSESSED and the finding reported: they return statically-known index columns and have no attached schema, so they are expected to be out of scope — say so explicitly rather than silently skipping them
sql.rs:271 delegates to the inner OptimizedTableImpl and needs no change — confirm, do not edit
forbidden: do not invent, fabricate, or default any column name — that is exactly the class #2000 and #2025 deleted. If there is no schema and no observed row, the honest answer is the empty set
do not make column_names() replace observed columns with declared ones — a table can legitimately carry columns the schema does not declare
do not change the trait method's signature

do not 'fix' the default impl's iter_records() cost in this PR — the CompactTable decompress-per-call concern is real and noted on the issue, but caching or a signature change is a separate design decision. Report it; do not implement it
do not touch stream_table_join.rs — it is the CONSUMER; if the fix requires changing it, that means the fix is in the wrong place
do not create a branch: the worktree is already on the branch velo-dispatch cut for you
stop_conditions: the reproduction does NOT return [] for a schema-attached, row-empty OptimizedTableImpl on current master — STOP and report; that is the premise of the issue

unioning the schema into the default impl breaks correlated-subquery inner-vs-outer classification (correlated_subquery_decorrelate.rs, select/subquery.rs) — STOP and report; that classification is what the default impl's doc block is about and a behaviour change there is a separate decision
more than ~10 pre-existing tests fail — STOP and report the list before changing any
